repairs.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
repairs.current_note: The usual *-ed* form for that same uneven tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays short and cool.
repairs.reader_said: 'The usual *-ed* form' is a frequency claim about which form is used, which we have no corpus to support; it also leans on 'that same' tearing from a note the reader cannot see.
repairs.axis: harm merely reported → damage shown in graphic bodily detail

synset_siblings.tone: The clipped form for flesh left with jagged edges, cool in shape even though the picture it raises is not.
The most violent of these: the jagged edges read as wreckage, the thing ruined rather than merely cut.
The plainest word for a ragged injured edge — it names the tearing and stops, where *mangled* piles on ruin.

whole_family.tone: The flat report that harm was done, holding back every picture of it that *mangled* insists on showing.
Here the marks stand as proof of what was come through, so the damage reads as standing earned rather than harm suffered.

whole_family.gloss: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
whole_family.tone: Names the bruise by its two colours, homely and concrete beside the graver *livid*.

whole_family.gloss: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
whole_family.tone: The same bruising, but heavy and grim, as if something has gone badly wrong under the skin, where *black-and-blue* stays almost homely.
Structural and bloodless: the joint has come apart, and the word says nothing at all about pain.
The exact term for a joint driven out of place, diagnostic where *disjointed* sounds merely come-apart.
The barest statement of the same parting at the joint — it neither winces nor diagnoses.
The most graphic member: the body opened and emptied, damage gone past anything that could still be called a wound.

whole_family.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
whole_family.tone: The softest word here for real physical injury: it suggests battle only a little and shows nothing of the wound.

whole_family.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
whole_family.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurt* for the same injury, dignifying the damage and letting the battlefield sit close without shutting out other harm.
